title: SO-F-04A Composition of the checks on the Admission external hook: one synchronous function of the shape the hook takes that runs the relationship check of SO-F-04, any other local check and the service checks of SO-F-08 in the order given, honours a degraded answer only from a service check, lets a refusal beat a degraded answer, never lets a degraded answer admit, and adds nothing to the steps or events of the Admission
request: Follow-up to the signed SO-F-04, written from the open follow-up row 'Two users of the Admission external hook' of docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md (relationshipGate of SO-F-04, pull request #368, and SO-F-08). Unsigned: a delta proposed for red-team review. It does not supersede SO-F-04 or SO-F-08 and does not edit them: SO-F-04 keeps its ten criteria and SO-F-08 keeps its nine, and this contract adds one function and the rules for composing checks. The id has no '.N' suffix because in this repository a '.N' id (SO-F-03.2, SO-F-09.2) is a superseding version; this is an additive follow-up, as SO-W-08C is to SO-W-08B. OWNER DECISIONS (1 Nov 2026, on pull request #374): (1) SO-F-04A owns composeExternal. PG-W-21B WP21-03 will cite SO-F-04A's composeExternal and will not define a second one; PG-W-21B is frozen pending the owner decision on ADR 8 and this contract does not edit it. (2) After a degraded answer the later checks keep running, but only to collect reasons. A degraded check never contributes to an admit: the overall answer is a denial, it fails closed, and the contract defines no hold (what a node does with a degraded denial, such as queueing the contribution, is SO-F-08 and is not specified here). (3) The hook stays synchronous, and nothing changes in the signed SO-F-03.3 Admission.admit: the only change to src/engine/federation/admission.mjs is the added export. RED-TEAM RESPONSE (1 Nov 2026, on pull request #374, in agreement with the owner decisions): (a) Order. The provisional order of the checks on the hook is the relationship check of SO-F-04 (relationshipGate) first, then the eligibility gate of PG-W-21B WP21-03 when it exists, then the service checks of SO-F-08 last, so that the cheap local checks refuse before a service is called. The eligibility gate is a plain check and never returns a degraded answer. The order is marked provisional pending ADR 8, and composeExternal does not impose it: it runs the order it is given. (b) Synchronous, and how a service fits. The adapter of SO-F-08 makes its asynchronous call before admit is called, caches the verdict by content_hash, and a synchronous service check, an entry { check, mayDegrade: true }, reads the cache; a cache miss is a refusal, neither a pass nor a degraded answer. Any future asynchronous admission is a separate method, admitAsync, with no await between the replay check and the append, so that the check of the mark and the append stay one step; it is not specified here, and nothing here makes Admission.admit asynchronous. This is the shape SO-F-08 is asked to meet; this contract builds none of it. (c) A degraded answer is honoured only from an entry marked as a service check ({ check, mayDegrade: true }). A degraded answer from any other check, and { ok: true, degraded: true } from any check, is a refusal. ADR 8 says a trust check that cannot run refuses, so no check but a service check may say 'could not decide'. WHAT A REFUSAL OR A DEGRADED ANSWER DOES NOT SAY: the external step runs before the signature, authority and replay steps, so an answer of the hook is a statement about the hook's checks only and says nothing about whether the node's own steps would pass. What SO-F-08 queues after a degraded answer has therefore not been judged by the node's own rules, and every item SO-F-08 queues must run every step again (format, external, signature, authority and replay) when it is released; no verdict from the time it was queued is reused. MERGE ORDER of the three specs of pull request #374, which touch the same files. Spec pull requests: #374 changes contracts/scope-one/manifest.json, docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md and docs/scope-one/WBS.md the way every spec-only pull request does, by adding rows and, for a superseded contract, two fields, so it and the other open spec pull request that does the same (SO-F-09.3, #373) take a plain merge of main in whichever order they land, keeping both sets of rows; no spec depends on that order. Build order: pull requests #358 (SO-F-03.3) and #368 (SO-F-04) first; then SO-F-03.4 (admission.mjs: the mark and the re-read; docs/FEDERATION.md, the paragraph that says per sender); then SO-F-04B, which needs SO-F-03.4 (admission.mjs: AdmissionSet, one registration in the constructor, one shared function for a rejected record); SO-F-04A depends on neither and may be built before or after (admission.mjs: composeExternal only). Each of the three edits src/engine/federation/admission.mjs, docs/FEDERATION.md, docs/MODULES.md and test/helpers/** in a different place, and the one built later merges the one built earlier. Sign order: SO-F-03.4 before SO-F-04B; SO-F-04A at any time. BASE: SO-F-04. The files this contract names exist only in pull request #368 (head 042d727: src/engine/federation/policy.mjs with relationshipGate, src/engine/federation/membership.mjs, test/helpers/federation-node.mjs) and in pull request #358 (SO-F-03.3: src/engine/federation/admission.mjs, whose constructor takes the optional external check), which is stacked under it. Neither was merged when this was written. Draft, red-team and sign this contract against a base that holds them, and build it after they merge; on main today the named test cannot load its helper and the check cannot run. This pull request is spec only. WHAT THE CODE DOES TODAY (read at 042d727): the external option of Admission is one optional synchronous function of the envelope that returns { ok: true } or { ok: false, code, reason }; it runs after the format step and before the signature, authority and replay steps; a refusal, a result that is not { ok: true } and a throw are each appended as federation.rejected with step external, with nothing of the payload. A throw gets the code external_failed and a reason that repeats the message of the throw, which can carry text of the payload; a result with no code gets external_refused; a returned promise is a result that is not { ok: true }, so it is a silent external_refused and, if it rejects, an unhandled rejection. relationshipGate returns a function of that shape. There is no way to hold two checks. SO-F-08 (signed, no code on main or on any branch of this repository) asks for an external admission service that runs before the node's own admission and before any append, and, when the service is unavailable, for degraded admission to be reported and the contribution to be queued and not admitted; the hook has no answer for 'unavailable' and treats it as a refusal. WHAT THIS CONTRACT SPECIFIES: composeExternal(...entries), exported from src/engine/federation/admission.mjs, returns one synchronous function of the hook's shape. An entry is a function (a plain check) or an object { check, mayDegrade: true } (a service check); anything else, and a mayDegrade that is present and not a boolean, is a TypeError when the composition is made, and the list is copied then. The checks run in the order given, each called with the envelope, and each answer is classified: (i) { ok: true } passes; keys other than ok on a pass are ignored and never copied into the answer; { ok: true, degraded: true } is a refusal. (ii) { ok: false, degraded: true } from a service check is a degraded answer; from any other entry it is a refusal with the code external_degraded_refused. (iii) Any other answer is a refusal: { ok: false, code, reason } keeps its own code (a string of at most 64 characters) and reason (at most 160), and a refusal that has no code gets the default code external_refused, the code the Admission itself gives; a value that is not an object (null, undefined, a string, an array) is a refusal with the default code. (iv) A throw is a refusal with the code external_check_failed and a fixed reason that never repeats the message of the throw. (v) A returned Promise, or any other thenable, is a refusal with the code external_check_async; the rejection of a returned promise is caught, so none is left unhandled. The first refusal ends the run and is the answer, and no later check is called. A degraded answer does not end the run: the later checks still run, only to collect reasons. The answer is built fresh, and carries only these keys and never a key of a check's own answer: ok; degraded, true, only when the answer is degraded; code and reason; position, the zero-based position in the list of the entry whose answer it is; and reasons, a list of { position, degraded, code, reason } for each degraded answer collected before the end of the run and for the refusal, if there is one. With a refusal the answer is that refusal, with degraded absent, and its position is its own; with no refusal and at least one degraded answer it is the first degraded answer, with degraded true; with every check passing it is { ok: true, reasons: [] }. A degraded answer never contributes to an admit: the answer is ok true only when every entry passed, whatever the order and however many entries pass. An empty list passes, and an Admission given it appends the same events as an Admission with no external option. The Admission gains no step, code or event, and Admission.admit and the constructor are not changed. INTERIM: today the Admission records any answer that is not ok true as federation.rejected with step external; SO-F-08 criterion 3 says a degraded contribution is queued and not admitted, so how the Admission records a degraded denial (the step, the event, a queue) is SO-F-08's and may change; this contract pins only that a degraded answer admits nothing, appends no federation.admitted and leaves nothing of the payload in the log. BOUNDARIES: (1) PG-W-21B (on main since pull request #371, unsigned, frozen pending the owner decision on ADR 8) names a composeExternal in task WP21-03, in src/engine/federation/trust-gate.mjs. By the owner decision above it will import the composeExternal of this contract from admission.mjs, in a later docs pull request, and will not define a second one; this contract does not edit PG-W-21B. ADR 8 (proposed) says a trust check that cannot run refuses, so a throw is a refusal here and no trust check can be marked to degrade; the degraded answer is for the admission service of SO-F-08 alone. (2) The trust adapter boundary is WP09-02 of PG-09.1 and the admission adapter is SO-F-08; this contract builds neither, and its tests use stand-in checks, not an SO-F-08 module that does not exist. (3) The hook stays synchronous, by the owner decision above, and the cache and admitAsync paragraphs above are the intended shape for SO-F-08, which specifies and builds them; changing Admission.admit to asynchronous is a change to a signed surface this contract does not make. (4) A signed contribution proves a key signed it; the composed check still skips no later step, so signature, authority and replay run after a pass. Provenance: written for this repository, not adapted from the fold. Settled decisions this contract follows (owner decision 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md): topology is local-first and the cloud is only a relay and a backup; every supported provider stands on equal footing and no work or tier depends on one; crdt-merge is reached only through the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs and this contract adds no merge engine to the core (ADR 6, decided); tiers follow docs/PRICING.md and federation stays a planned capability of the tiers above Personal, by contacting us, never a price cell. Open decisions this contract does not make: ADR 7 (memory and project-state authority, proposed) is cited and not decided, and this contract adds no store and no event type beyond the two the Admission already writes (federation.admitted and federation.rejected), so there is one store under the vault and no second database; ADR 2 (id and event ordering, open) keeps its safe default, the order of the operation log, and this contract adds no sequence of its own; ADR 3 (lease semantics, open) is not touched, and nothing here is a lease or a role-by-action rule. ADR 5 (permission matrix, open) and SO-A-05 (the decision and blocker queue; the place where an admission decision would be raised, and who may answer one, stays provisional until both are decided) are not touched: nothing here raises a decision or a blocker, and a degraded answer is not one. ADR 8 (trust governance in the federated model, proposed, pending owner decision; docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md and docs/scope-one/design/trust-governance.md) is not decided or pre-empted: nothing here defines a trust record, a trust gate, who may grant trust or how a revocation propagates, and no criterion reads trust.

tasks.description: The Admission of SO-F-03.3 takes one optional check, and two things need it: the relationship check of SO-F-04 and the external admission service of SO-F-08. This contract gives a node a way to hold both without changing the Admission: one function that runs a list of checks and answers in the hook's own shape. It also gives the hook the one answer the service needs and the hook lacks, 'could not decide', allows it to a service check alone, and fixes what it does: it never helps to admit, it fails closed, and the reasons of the checks that ran after it are kept so that a node can say why. It specifies no service, no trust check, no hold, no queue and no transport, and it changes no step of the Admission and not Admission.admit. The named test imports each module of the contract by namespace (import * as ns), never by name, and asserts that the export it needs is a function or a class before it uses it, so that on the base the red run fails on an assertion; the red-green check treats a load error as BLOCKED, not as red.

criteria.statement: composeExternal is a function exported from src/engine/federation/admission.mjs and returns one synchronous function of the shape the Admission external option takes: it runs the checks in the order given and answers with the first refusal (its code and reason, and its position), and a later check is not called; a function and an object { check, mayDegrade } are the entries, and any other entry, and a mayDegrade that is not a boolean, is a TypeError when the composition is made, and a later change to the caller's list has no effect; a throw is a refusal with the code external_check_failed whose reason is fixed and does not contain the message of the throw; a returned Promise and a returned thenable (also one whose then throws) are each refused with the code external_check_async, and the rejection of a returned promise is caught, so that no unhandledRejection is raised (the test listens for it across two event-loop turns); a value that is not an object (null, undefined, a string, an array), an object with no ok, ok as a string and { ok: false } with no code are refusals, and each that gives no code of its own gets the default code external_refused; { ok: true } with extra keys is a pass and the answer holds none of them; an empty list answers { ok: true, reasons: [] }; the test fails by assertion on the base

stop_rules: Stop and post BLOCKED when a criterion cannot pass without weakening a test, skipping a test or relaxing an assertion.
Stop and ask when the work would name a client product, a person, a server or a seat in repository text; the client names live in docs/CLIENTS.md only.
Stop when the work would add a runtime dependency, a model call, a network call at install or start, a second store for project state, or any reporting that is not opt-in and off by default.
Stop when the work would move convergence logic into the core, vendor the engine, or add a merge engine beside the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs.

Stop when the work would implement a federation, replication, trust, admission or computation feature beyond the specification, schema, validator and conformance test the contract names; the product keeps the planned label on it.

Stop and ask when the work would change a step, a code or an event type of the Admission, change Admission.admit or its constructor, edit a file of SO-F-03.3 beyond adding the one export, or define a hold, a queue or how the Admission handles a degraded answer: that is SO-F-08.

Stop and ask when the work would let a degraded answer, or any answer other than every check passing, produce an admit, or would honour a degraded answer from an entry that is not marked { check, mayDegrade: true }; the composition fails closed.

Stop and ask when the work would define a trust record, a trust check or the place of one in the order beyond the provisional order stated here, edit PG-W-21B, or decide any open ADR (ADR 8 above all); PG-W-21B is frozen pending the owner and cites this contract's composeExternal, not the other way round.

Stop and ask when the work would make the hook asynchronous, add admitAsync, add a call to a service, a timer, a clock, a wait or a store of its own to composeExternal, or add a second definition of composeExternal beside the one this contract names.
Stop and ask when the work would treat an answer of the hook as a judgement of the node's own steps, or let anything queued after a degraded answer skip a step when it is released.
If any criterion fails after the fix: STOP, report the measured result, the failing check and file:line. Do not start the next task.
If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.
